en: Dependent on a state that is not a fetter, non-visible, and impinging, there arises a state that is not a fetter, visible, and impinging, by way of root condition...
(Three questions. Abbreviated. Three for root; three for predominance...
pe ... one for result... pe ... three for non-disappearance.
Dependent on a state that is not-yoked, visible, and impinging, there arises a state that is not-yoked, visible, and impinging by way of root condition. (Abbreviated.
Three for root; three for predominance … pe … one for result … pe … three for non-disappearance.
Dependent on a state that is not-flood, not-visible, and not-impinging, there arises a state that is not-flood, visible, and impinging by way of root condition. (Abbreviated.)

With respect to the root condition, there are three; with respect to the predominance condition, there are three ... pe ... with respect to the resultant condition, there is one ... pe ... with respect to the non-disappearance condition, there are three.

Dependent on a state that is neither-yoked-nor-visible-and-reactive, a state that is yoked-visible-and-reactive arises by way of the root condition. (Abbreviated. With respect to the root condition, there are three; with respect to the predominance condition, there are three ...
pe ... with respect to the resultant condition, there is one ... pe ... with respect to the non-disappearance condition, there are three.

Dependent on a state that is not an hindrance (*anīvaraṇa*), visible (*sanidassana*), and impinging (*sappaṭigha*), there arises a state that is not an hindrance, visible, and impinging, by way of root-condition (*hetu-paccaya*).

(Abbreviated. Under root [condition] there are three; under predominance (*adhipati*) there are three ... pe ... under resultant (*vipāka*) there is one ... pe ... under non-disappearance (*avigata*) there are three.

Dependent on a state that is not associated with lust (*aparāmāsa*), visible, and impinging, there arises a state that is not associated with lust, visible, and impinging, by way of root-condition. (Abbreviated.)

With respect to the root condition, there are three; with respect to the predominance condition, there are three ... pe ... with respect to the result condition, there is one ... pe ... with respect to the non-disappearance condition, there are three.
